extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent applicants/practitioners (prosecution attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_short: patent prosecution suspension and reply rules
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards from the MPEP governing (A) requests and Office actions to suspend or defer examination (37 CFR 1.103(b)-(f)), termination of suspensions, and Office-initiated suspensions, and (B) computation of reply periods, abandonment rules, and extensions under 35 U.S.C. 133, 37 CFR 1.135 and 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension under 37 CFR 1.103(a) — applicant-initiated suspension period and continuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Action by the Office is suspended on this application under 37 CFR 1.103(a) for a period of [2] months. At the end of this period, applicant is required to notify the examiner and request continuance of prosecution or a further suspension. See MPEP § 709.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: Maximum period for suspension is 6 months. Only the Technology Center Director can grant second or subsequent suspensions; such approval must appear on the Office letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for suspension denied when outstanding applicant reply exists
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s request for suspension of action in this application under 37 CFR 1.103(a) is denied as being improper. Action cannot be suspended in an application awaiting a reply by the applicant. See MPEP § 709.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form language to deny. The presence of a pending applicant reply precludes grant of suspension under 1.103(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for suspension request filed with CPA or RCE (37 CFR 1.103(b)/(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may request a suspension of action by the Office under 37 CFR 1.103(b) or (c) for a period not exceeding three months in a CPA filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d) or in an RCE filed under 37 CFR 1.114. The request for suspension must be filed at the time of filing of the CPA or RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not grant the requested suspension unless: (A) the request is filed with the filing of a CPA or an RCE (may use check box on transmittal forms or separate paper); (1) if filed with an RCE, the RCE must be in compliance with 37 CFR 1.114 (accompanied by a submission and the fee set forth in 1.17(e)); (2) if filed with a CPA, a filing date must be assigned to the CPA; (B) the request should specify the period in whole months (maximum 3 months; if unspecified or >3, Office will assume 3 months); (C) the request must include the processing fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(i). Note: RCE filing fee cannot be deferred and the suspension request cannot substitute for the required submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of missing parts for CPA when filing date is granted
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office assigns a filing date to the CPA, the request for suspension will be processed even if the CPA was not accompanied by the CPA filing fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension acts to suspend the first Office action but does not affect processing for a missing part. Applicant will be given 2 months from notification to pay the CPA filing fee and surcharge set forth in 37 CFR 1.16(e). Failure to pay within 2 months will result in abandonment of the CPA. Suspension period starts on the filing date of the CPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper RCE or CPA (no filing date) — suspension not recognized
rubrics_metrics.description: If the CPA or the RCE is improper (e.g., filing date not accorded, RCE filed without a submission or RCE fee), the Office will not recognize the request for suspension, and action by the Office will not be suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Notice of Improper CPA Filing or Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination will be sent. Time periods set in previous Office communications continue to run. The suspension request will not be processed until the Office accords a filing date or receives a proper RCE; applicant should resubmit the suspension request if/when they file another RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper request for suspension (untimely or missing fee) — denial and treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: If the CPA or RCE is properly filed, but the request for suspension is improper (e.g., untimely or without the processing fee 37 CFR 1.17(i)), action by the Office will not be suspended on the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will process the CPA or RCE and place the application on the examiner’s docket. The examiner will notify the applicant of the denial in the next Office communication using form paragraph ¶ 7.56.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper request for suspension (CPA/RCE) — processing and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: If the CPA or the RCE and the request for suspension of action are proper, the Office’s technical support staff will process the CPA or RCE, and the request for suspension of action. A notification of the approval of the request for suspension will be sent to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application will be placed in suspension status until the end of the suspension period. The suspension request acts to suspend a first Office action by the examiner. Once the suspension period has expired, the application will be placed on the examiner’s docket for further prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for deferral of examination under 37 CFR 1.103(d) — basic rule
rubrics_metrics.description: In new applications, applicants may request a deferral of examination under 37 CFR 1.103(d) for a period not extending beyond three years from the earliest filing date for which a benefit is claimed. The request must be filed before the Office issues an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension will start on the day the Office grants the request for deferral; once granted the application will not be taken up by the examiner until the suspension period expires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements to request deferral of examination (37 CFR 1.103(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/37 may be used. A request must include: (A) a period of suspension in whole months not extending beyond three years from the earliest effective filing date (if blank or exceeds max, Office will assume max); (B) the publication fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.18(d); and (C) the processing fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not grant deferral unless all the specified conditions are met (see next entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for granting deferral of examination (1.103(d) — application eligibility and prerequisites)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will grant a deferral only if the following conditions are met: (A) the application must be (1) an original utility or plant application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) or (2) an application resulting from entry of the national stage after compliance with 37 CFR 1.495 (cannot be design, reissue, or a CPA under 1.53(d)); (B) the application must be filed on or after November 29, 2000, or if filed before that date the applicant must submit a request for voluntary publication, the voluntary publication fee, an EFS-compliant copy, and the confirmation number; (C) applicant must not have an extant nonpublication request under 1.213(a) (or must file a rescission under 1.213(b)); (D) the application must be in condition for publication as provided in 1.211(c); and (E) the Office must not have issued an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any condition is lacking, the deferral request is improper and will be denied with reasons (use form ¶ 7.56.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper request for deferral — denial and required insertions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request for deferral is improper, notify applicant of denial using ¶ 7.56.02 and insert the filing date and reason(s) for denying the request (e.g., nonpublication request not rescinded; a first Office action has been issued; applicant did not submit a request for voluntary publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supervisory patent examiner approval is required for grant; use ¶ 7.54.01 for grant notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of suspension of action at applicant request
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for termination of a suspension of action will be effective when an appropriate official of the Office takes action thereon. If the request properly identifies the application and the period of suspension has not expired when the Office acts, the Office will terminate the suspension and place the application on the examiner’s docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledgment should be sent to applicant using form ¶ 7.54.02 (insert filing date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office-initiated suspension — avoid, limits, and approvals (37 CFR 1.103(e),(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension of action at the initiative of the Office should be avoided if possible. 37 CFR 1.103(e) provides that the Office will notify applicant if the Office suspends action on its own initiative. Every Office-initiated suspension will be limited to a maximum of 6 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner may grant an initial suspension on his/her own initiative for a maximum of 6 months. The Office must mail a notification for each Office-initiated suspension including the suspension period. When the period expires, the examiner should take up action or seek alternatives (e.g., find another reference). If a second or subsequent suspension is necessary, the examiner must obtain the TC Director's approval and the TC Director must sign the notification. Suspension under 1.103(f) is decided by the TC Director of work group 3640.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs for Office-initiated suspensions (examples ¶ 7.52 and ¶ 7.53)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standardized form paragraphs to notify applicants of Office-initiated suspensions such as 'Suspension of Action, Awaiting New Reference' (¶ 7.52) and 'Suspension of Action, Possible Interference' (¶ 7.53).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs include the suspension period [1] months and examiner notes reminding that maximum period is six months and TC Director must approve/sign second or subsequent suspensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling overlapping applications by same applicant/assignee
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should not consider ex parte questions which are pending before the Office in inter partes proceedings involving the same applicant. Where one of several applications with overlapping claims gets into an interference, better practice is to reject claims in the related (outside) application over the counts of the interference and suspend prosecution pending final determination of priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant wishes to prosecute the outside application and presents good reasons, prosecution should be continued. See MPEP § 2315.01 and § 804.03 for supporting authorities/cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory period for reply and abandonment rules (35 U.S.C. 133; 37 CFR 1.135)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon failure to prosecute the application within six months after any action therein (or shorter time fixed by Director, not less than 30 days), the application shall be regarded as abandoned unless delay was unavoidable. 37 CFR 1.135 provides that if no reply is filed within the time set under 1.134 and 1.136 the application will become abandoned unless an Office action indicates otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.135(b): admission or refusal to admit any amendment after final rejection or any amendment not responsive to the last action will not save the application from abandonment. 1.135(c) allows examiner discretion to accept a bona fide, substantially complete reply that inadvertently omits something and give a shortened period (generally 1 month) to supply the omission to avoid abandonment. Examiner may waive deficiencies that do not preclude action on the merits or may require supply of omission; whether to give 1-month is within examiner discretion and may be withheld if omission appears intentional/abusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of statutory period for reply
rubrics_metrics.description: The actual time taken for reply is computed from the date stamped or printed on the Office action to the date of receipt by the Office of applicant’s reply; no cognizance is taken of fractions of a day and the reply is due on the corresponding day of the month (e.g., 6 months later).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 1-month extension extends to the corresponding date next month. If the due date falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday and the period is a 30-day period, filing on the next succeeding business day is timely. The Office date stamp on the reply paper determines receipt date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory periods and when used (37 CFR 1.136 authority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.136, an applicant required to reply within a nonstatutory or shortened statutory time period may extend the time under specified rules; shortened statutory periods (not less than 30 days) are used in many situations and vary with the type of reply required (e.g., 1 month, 2 months, 3 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: 1 month (not less than 30 days) when a bona fide reply includes an inadvertent omission (see MPEP § 710.01 and § 714.03); 2 months for Ex parte Quayle or winning party in a terminated interference; 3 months to reply to any Office action on the merits. Shortened periods should be prominently indicated on the first page of actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136 — general rules
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.136(a)(1): Applicant may extend a shortened/nonstatutory time up to the earlier of the maximum statutory period or five months after the time set for reply, if a petition and fee under 1.17(a) are filed, unless exceptions apply (e.g., notified otherwise in Office action, reply brief under 1.193(b), appeals, interference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date of filing the petition and fee determines the period of extension and the fee amount. Filing authorizations or fees may be treated as a constructive petition. If (a) is not available, 1.136(b) permits extension only for sufficient cause and reasonable time filed on or before the due date, and no extension can carry the date beyond the statutory maximum. Certain time periods set in a Notice of Allowability are not extendable under 1.136(c) (e.g., periods for submitting an oath or declaration 1.63, formal drawings 1.85(c), or deposits 1.809(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specified time limits (non-abandonment consequences) — when used and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain examiner-set specified time limits require applicant to take action within a set time where failure results in a consequence other than abandonment (e.g., decision rendered without applicant's input, omitted IDS parts placed in file but not considered, authorization to cancel claims to non-elected invention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (A) petition under 1.14(e) for public access — Office may give usually 3 weeks to state objections; failure will result in decision without applicant's objections but not affect prosecution; (B) IDS that complies with 1.97 but omits parts — examiner may set 1-month to complete IDS; failure will not result in abandonment but omitted content will not be considered; (C) allowable application containing traverse of restriction — may be given e.g., 1 month to cancel nonelected claims or petition under 1.144; failure treated as authorization to cancel claims and application passed to issue.
